title: The storm was real.
paragraphs: The storm was real.
These were not inexperienced men panicking over small waves.
Several of the disciples were fishermen who had lived their lives on that sea.
If they were afraid, the storm was serious.

Waves were crashing into the boat.
Water was filling the hull.
The wind was violent.
And Jesus was asleep.
Imagine the moment.

The boat shaking.
Thunder cracking across the sky.
Disciples shouting over the wind.
And at the back of the boat… the Son of God is resting.
Eventually they wake Him with frustration:
“Teacher, don’t you care that we are perishing?”
Then Jesus stands.
He speaks three words to the storm.
“Peace. Be still.”
And instantly the sea obeys.
But the most revealing part of the story comes next.
Jesus asks them a question.
“Why are you so afraid?”
The real issue wasn’t the storm.
It was their perspective.
They saw the storm as the most powerful thing in their situation.
Jesus saw His Father as the most powerful.
Many of us live in the same tension today.
We panic when waves rise in our lives.

Financial storms.
Health storms.
Family storms.
Uncertain futures.
But this story reminds us of something powerful:
The presence of a storm does not mean the absence of God.
And if Jesus is in the boat, the storm is not the final authority.
Three truths stand out from this moment:

• God’s peace is not controlled by circumstances.
• Faith sees beyond the waves to the One who rules them.
• The One who can calm the storm can also calm the heart.
Sometimes the greatest miracle is not that Jesus calms the storm.
Sometimes the miracle is that He teaches us how to rest in it.
